title: POC Weekly - Latency Convergence Huddle
summary: Weekly sync focused on bringing TTFT and streaming variance under the POC SLOs. Reviewed last week's bench runs (microburst and seqlen sweep), agreed on kernel hedging for short vs long sequences, and decided next bench: deterministic microburst + KV-cache warmup. Action owner matrix updated; Redwood to send kernel-selection spreadsheet and updated security snapshot.
action_items: Marco Ruiz: share kernel-decision spreadsheet and perf profiles by 2026-12-04
Priya Reddy: provide production sequence-length histogram and 95/99% seqlen buckets by 2026-12-06
Sophie Lee: send updated security snapshot and SSO/SAML notes by 2026-12-05
Tomás Alvarez: run deterministic microburst bench with KV warmup (3 runs) and upload logs by 2026-12-09
Jordan Myers: enable trace sampling hook for the next bench and share trace ids by 2026-12-09
next_steps: Redwood to propose kernel hedging rules and routing policy config
Customer to run deterministic microburst + KV warmup and share results
Schedule 1-hour deep-dive on hedging policy (week of 2026-12-14)
Exchange SSO/KMS docs and updated SOC2 snapshot
transcript:
[15:00] Sophie Lee: Alright everyone, thanks for jumping on. We're on for 50 minutes today, is that right?
[15:01] Priya Reddy: Yep should be fine. We wanted to focus on the TTFT spikes we saw on Tuesday — particularly the microburst at 09:13 UTC.
[15:02] Marco Ruiz: I pulled the bench results, um, last night. The short path kernel does very well for seqlen < 64 but once you get into 128+ we see tail noise because of kernel fallback.
[15:03] Tomás Alvarez: Right, and to add — our traffic has a bimodal distribution, like 60% under 40 tokens and another 25% in the 300–700 token range. That makes fixed batching rough.
[15:05] Aisha N’Dour: Quick clarification: when you say "kernel fallback" are we talking about an automatic runtime switch or a manual route?
[15:05] Marco Ruiz: It's runtime, but we can bias routing earlier — so policy decides whether to route to quantized fastpath or to higher-memory kernel that handles long seqlen.
[15:06] Jordan Myers: (background) yeah, also note our load balancer did some reconfig last week which might correlate.
[15:07] Sophie Lee: Good point. Let's separate infra noise vs model path issues. Tomás, the bench you ran — did you include KV-cache warmup?
[15:08] Tomás Alvarez: No, we did cold starts only. We wanted to see worst-case TTFT baseline. But we can re-run with warmup.
[15:10] Sophie Lee: Okay perfect. Marco, you mentioned hedging rules — can you summarize the proposal?
[15:11] Marco Ruiz: Sure. Proposal A: for seqlen < 64 use FastKernel-V2 with continuous batching and prefix caching. Proposal B: for 64–256 try FastKernel-V2 but with microburst padding + small hedging window to a HighMemory kernel when latency approaches SLO. Proposal C: >256 default to HighMemory kernel. We'll also add a 30ms early-fallback probe for streaming handshakes.
[15:13] Priya Reddy: That sounds promising; how does that affect cost? Our CFO is sensitive to switching to HighMemory kernel.
[15:14] Marco Ruiz: Hedging increases token-cost because you might keep additional CUDA contexts or do parallel probes but if we set conservative thresholds the cost delta is ~6–8% for mixed traffic; for you with bimodal pattern it'll be more like 10–12% worst-case.
[15:15] Lena Chu: Is there a simple knob we can expose in the config to toggle hedging intensity? We don't want to rework infra quickly.
[15:16] Sophie Lee: Yes, Redwood can expose hedging intensity and SLO margins as config. We can ship a spreadsheet with expected cost delta by bucket and an easy toggle.
[15:18] Tomás Alvarez: About streaming — we saw jitter in the handshake causing early bytes to be delayed about 20–40ms intermittently. Any ideas?
[15:19] Marco Ruiz: Two things: buffer sizing and early-first-token priority. We can bias priority to prefix-first-token streams, and tune the streaming ACKs to reduce microburst queueing. Also, ensure kernel selection decision happens before the streaming handshake completes so the runtime doesn't requeue.
[15:21] Priya Reddy: That pre-selection sounds fragile if our load balancer shifts route mid-request.
[15:22] Aisha N’Dour: We handle that by binding a sticky session to the model instance for the stream; if LB moves, the runtime will detect and rehydrate KV cache, but that costs a re-priming penalty.
[15:23] Jordan Myers: How big is the re-prime penalty?
[15:24] Marco Ruiz: For your models we measured ~120–180ms for KV rehydrate on those long contexts, with smaller cost for shorter seqlens. The idea is to avoid rebinds where possible.
[15:25] Sophie Lee: For the bench plan: Tomás, you run deterministic microburst (3 runs) with KV warmup and sticky LB on; we want traces. Jordan, enable trace sampling hook and share IDs.
[15:26] Tomás Alvarez: Got it. We'll pin the clients to a single AZ for the run.
[15:27] Priya Reddy: Security/compliance quick question — if we enable sticky sessions and keep certain contexts in-memory, does that affect PII audit expectations?
[15:28] Sophie Lee: Good question. It shouldn't change retention or PII handling; KV cache is transient and not persisted. We'll send our security snapshot and KMS/SAML docs.
[15:29] Lena Chu: Also send the contract note about audit logs retention, we have compliance review next week.
[15:30] Sophie Lee: We'll include retention tables. Marco, any remaining perf experiments you'd like Glyph to run?
[15:31] Marco Ruiz: Two quick ones: 1) microburst with and without autoscaler headroom; 2) a seqlen-routing test where we artificially label requests to force routes and measure warm/cold mix.
[15:33] Tomás Alvarez: We can do both. The seqlen routing test will be useful to verify the cost vs latency knobs.
[15:34] Aisha N’Dour: Minor transcript note — sometimes the export renames Redwood functions like "KV cache" into odd tokens, don't mind typos.
[15:35] Sophie Lee: (laughs) yep Fireflies is creative. Any blockers?
[15:36] Priya Reddy: Main blocker is time — Tomás needs to schedule bench runs during our low-traffic window. We'll aim for Friday evening PST.
[15:37] Jordan Myers: Also need the hedging spreadsheet to decide thresholds before we run.
[15:38] Marco Ruiz: I'll get the spreadsheet over by Friday EOD. It will include cost modeling and recommended defaults.
[15:40] Sophie Lee: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners — Marco spreadsheet, Tomás bench + logs, Jordan traces, Sophie security docs, Priya will send seqlen histogram. Then we'll meet for a 60-minute hedging deep-dive week of Dec 14.
[15:41] Lena Chu: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[15:42] Sophie Lee: Thank you all, I'll create calendar invite for the deep-dive and upload notes.
[15:43] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has small ASR mistakes (proper nouns a bit off). Some speaker labels may mismatch where multiple people speak over each other.
